subject: Request: Trial extension & sandbox credits — integration sprint hold
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@brightlane.io>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@brightlane.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick check-in on pilot — blockers on our side

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We spun up the sandbox and started wiring the webhook adapter, but hit a blocker in our adapter layer that’s eating time — our eng lead expects at least two more sprints (4–6 weeks) before the connector will be stable.

We still want to complete the pilot with Redwood — the model responses look promising — but we need a bit more runway to finish the integration and produce the evaluation prompts we discussed. Can we get a 45-day extension on the trial window and a small sandbox credit top-up (approx. $3,000) to keep the environment active while we unblock? I’ve attached a short snapshot of the integration logs that show the throttling pattern we’re seeing.

Appreciate any flexibility you can provide — it will help keep momentum.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform
Brightlane Labs

Attachments: integration-log-snapshot.txt (plain text, 45 KB)
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@brightlane.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick check-in on pilot — blockers on our side

Hi Samir — thanks for the log and the clear summary. Sorry to hear the adapter is stuck; we’ve seen the same pattern before and it usually lands in a three- to four-week engineering effort.

I’m looping in Laura (revops) and Ben (AE) to see what runway/credit flexibility we can offer. We want Brightlane to get a fair shake to complete the evaluation; please give us a few hours and we’ll follow up with a proposed plan.

—Hiro
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick check-in on pilot — blockers on our side

Thanks for the ping. Quick internal note on policy and precedent: we typically grant 30 days of trial extension plus a sandbox credit top-up for integration blockers when engineering work is the primary cause. Larger requests (> $2k) go through a one-off credit approval and we document as a "make-good" in the deal.

Numbers: to be conservative, I can approve a $2,500 sandbox top-up from the standard discretionary fund without Sales Ops sign-off. Anything above that needs Revenue Ops manager review. For the timebox, 30 days extension is within autonomous approval; extensions beyond that (45+ days) should be tied to a mutually agreed plan (updated MAP) and a short statement of expected engineering milestones.

Suggested path:
- Approve 30-day extension + $2.5k credit today to keep their sandbox active.
- AE to confirm the new MAP and milestone dates; if Brightlane can commit to targeted checkpoints at 14 and 30 days, we’ll reconsider an additional 15-day extension + another $500 credit after the first checkpoint.

If you want, I’ll draft the short approval memo and the note to attach to the HubSpot deal.

—Laura
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: approval-notes-redwood.pdf (approval summary stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick check-in on pilot — blockers on our side

Laura — that sounds reasonable. Two small notes from the AE side:
1) Brightlane is an ARR motion opportunity we’d like to keep warm; they’ve already scheduled a product review with their CTO for mid-July. A 45-day runway will get them past that meeting and increase the probability of conversion.
2) If we can offer the initial 30-day + $2.5k top-up immediately and commit to revisiting after the 14-day checkpoint, I’ll get Samir to agree to milestone dates and a light quarterly roadmap excerpt for the deal file.

I’m good with Laura’s approval path — please go ahead and post the approval note so we can communicate it.

—Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@brightlane.io>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@brightlane.io>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick check-in on pilot — blockers on our side

Samir — good news. We’ll do the following to keep you moving:

1) Trial window extended by 30 days (effective immediately).
2) Sandbox credit top-up: $2,500 applied to your Brightlane sandbox account.
3) Checkpoint plan: target check-ins at 14 and 30 days from today. If Brightlane meets the 14-day milestone (basic adapter stability + sample webhook runs), we’ll review for an additional 15-day extension and a $500 supplement.

I’ve attached a short approval memo and linked the HubSpot deal for your records. If you’re comfortable with the checkpoints, Ben will update the MAP and we’ll send a one-line addendum to the trial terms for signatures (no legal redline expected).

Thanks for the quick update — reach out if the eng team needs a runbook or a pairing session; I can arrange a short troubleshooting slot with one of our integration engineers.

Best,
Hiro
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: approval-notes-redwood.pdf
